relationships.subject: MMPs
relationships.evidence_quote: MMPs have been implicated and lead to the disassembly of TJPs, resulting in disruption to the BBB/BSCB.

relationships.subject: neutrophils
relationships.evidence_quote: Neutrophils lead to the release of matrix metalloproteinases, neutrophil extracellular traps, and other proinflammatory mediators

relationships.subject: nociceptive signaling
relationships.evidence_quote: Nociceptive signaling results in a disruption to both central and peripheral barriers.

relationships.subject: glibenclamide
relationships.evidence_quote: glibenclamide and glyburide, have been shown to block the SUR1-Trpm4 channel

key_findings: Review: BBB/BSCB tight junction disruption after neural injury is driven by pain, inflammation, coagulopathy, MMPs and progressive hemorrhagic necrosis (SUR1-Trpm4)
Clinical translation: sulfonylureas, tranexamic acid, AAV-based CLDN-5 and Gpr124 strategies explored for barrier preservation
